Done. I diagnosed the problem and produced a verified, self-contained solution.

## What I found

The task (`/workspace/problem.json`) has **no test harness or required signature**, so I grounded the implementation in PostgreSQL's actual source rather than guessing. I fetched `src/backend/storage/lmgr/predicate.c` and implemented the semantics of `PreCommit_CheckForSerializationFailure()` and the `SXACT_FLAG_READ_ONLY` handling exactly.

## Root causes of the hard parts

1. **Snapshot-relative edges** — `R --rw--> W` exists only when `W` writes something `R` read **and** `W.commit >= R.begin` (invisible writer). This is the boundary most implementations get wrong.
2. **Dangerous structure, not any cycle** — only `Tin --rw--> Tpivot --rw--> Tout` with `Tout` committing first matters.
3. **First-committer-wins** — commit order decides the victim (classic write-skew 2-cycle aborts the *second* committer).
4. **Read-only far transactions** are excluded, otherwise PG would abort transactions it actually keeps.
5. **The pivot is doomed** (not the early committer), then aborts at its own commit point.

## Deliverables (in `/workspace`)

- **`solution.md`** — the required markdown: title, root-cause analysis, input model, algorithm, full embedded code, certificate format, and a verification section.
- **`ssi.py`** — reference implementation with a `verify()` function that independently re-derives the rw edges, pivots, dangerous triples, cycle witness, and abort set.
- **`tests.py`** — 9-scenario matrix.

## Verification

All tests pass, covering write skew in both commit orders, disjoint/no-anomaly schedules, read-only transactions, a read-only `Tin`, a non-read-only 3-node dangerous structure, all six commit orders of a 3-cycle, snapshot visibility, and JSON/CLI round-trip. I also re-extracted the code block from the markdown itself and ran it to confirm the document is executable as written — it produced `aborts: [2]` and passed `verify()`.

signatures.description: Implement PostgreSQL-style Serializable Snapshot Isolation conflict analysis over a supplied transaction schedule: build the rw-antidependency graph from read/write dependencies and snapshot boundaries, then decide whether a dangerous structure exists (a cycle with two or more consecutive rw-antidependency edges and a pivot transaction whose early commit closes the anomaly). Emit the exact set of transactions PostgreSQL would abort, ordered by commit time then pid, together with a machine-checkable certificate listing the antidependency edges and the cycle witness. Must handle read-only transactions, mutually opposing rw edges between a pair, and schedules with no anomaly (empty abort set).
